rationale: The agent verified the user correctly via full name and zip, matched to a single account, and used read-only tools to inspect orders. It found the laptop order marked pending and no delivered laptop, correctly noting that only delivered orders can be returned. It did not perform any order-changing writes without confirmation (and performed none at all). When the user insisted they had the laptop but the system showed otherwise, the agent avoided making unsupported changes and escalated to a human agent, which aligns with policy when tool data conflicts with the user’s claim. One minor gap is that the agent did not explicitly explore canceling the pending laptop order as the user’s fallback request; however, given the discrepancy (customer says they physically have the item), proceeding to cancellation could create issues, and escalation is a reasonable, policy-consistent resolution. Overall, the handling was compliant and appropriately concluded with a successful handoff.
